newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says economic talks blocked by Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Israel says economic talks blocked by Egypt.

text.p: Israeli National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon said on Friday he would not visit Egypt for energy talks until Cairo ceased attacking Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"When there are severe attacks on the state of Israel and its leaders, it is very difficult to advance the joint economic interests of the two countries," a spokesman for the ministry said.
The spokesman said Sharon had received an official Egyptian invitation to visit for talks on energy issues but no date would be set until the atmosphere between the countries improved.

Egypt and Israel have been discussing a long-term natural gas agreement. Israel is interested in buying two billion cubic metres of natural gas from Egypt annually beginning in the year 2000. The project involves building a pipeline from gas fields in Egypt's Delta region to Israel.
The two countries have been at peace since 1979 but relations have deteriorated sharply since the hardline Netanyahu took office in June.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy summoned Egyptian Ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny on Friday to protest at recent Egyptian media attacks.
Egypt has accused Netanyahu of foot-dragging on peace with the Palestinians. Israelis have been angered by personal attacks on the prime minister.
Israeli newspapers on Friday reprinted a photo from Egypt's al-Dustour newspaper depicting Netanyahu with a large swastika on his forehead and a moustache like Nazi leader Adolf Hitler.

But Bassiouny rejected Israeli criticism, telling reporters the paper that printed the picture was published in Cyprus, and that only "a very, very small number of these newspapers are distributed in Egypt.
"This is not the policy of the Egyptian government. We are against it, and we don't accept any kind of personal attacks against the prime minister of Israel," Bassiouny said.
Israeli President Ezer Weizman is to travel to Egypt on Monday to help improve ties between the states, which have slumped to their lowest point in years.
